topPRs.title: refactor(op-e2e): run L2 EL on op-reth by default
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## What & why

op-geth is deprecated and cannot seal Karst/Osaka blocks, so the interop super-cannon tests in `op-e2e/faultproofs` hang: op-node requests `engine_getPayloadV5` once Karst is active, op-geth rejects it with `Unsupported fork`, block production stalls, and the `op-e2e-cannon-tests` (develop-fault-proofs) job times out. This switches op-e2e's L2 execution layer to **op-reth** (the official Karst EL).

- New `op-e2e/e2eutils/reth`: external op-reth process implementing `services.EthInstance`.
- New `op-e2e/e2eutils/el`: single L2 EL construction seam selecting op-geth or op-reth via `OP_E2E_L2_EL_KIND` (**default op-reth**); fails fast if geth-only options are requested against op-reth.
- `e2esys` and the interop `SuperSystem` construct the L2 EL through `el.InitL2`. Sentry tx-forwarding (`RollupSequencerHTTP`) maps to op-reth `--rollup.sequencer-http`.
- op-geth-specific tests pinned to op-geth via `WithL2ELKind`: legacy pending block, DA throttling, txpool gossip, `op-e2e/opgeth/*`.
- CI: `go-tests-short` and `go-tests-full` consume the op-reth binary already persisted to the workspace by `rust-workspace-binaries` (no extra build).
- **L1 stays op-geth.** `op-e2e/actions` (in-process engine emulator) is unchanged.

topPRs.title: feat(op-challenger): add --format json to list-claims and list-games
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Description

`op-challenger list-claims` and `list-games` only emitted human-formatted tables with truncated (`TerminalString`) values, awkward to consume programmatically or from an AI agent. This adds a `--format` flag (`text` default, `json`) to **both** subcommands.

Each builds a structured report once and renders it:
- **list-claims** json carries the full claim value, exact bond (`bondWei` + `bondEth`), unix timestamp, clock-used seconds, and structured resolution fields (`counteredBy`/`resolved`/`resolvableAt`).
- **list-games** json carries the full output root, unix + RFC3339 timestamps, and typed game fields (`index`, `gameType`, `l2BlockNumber`, `claimCount`, `status`).

JSON was chosen over CSV as the single structured format — it's typed, preserves nested fields, and parses robustly for agents/scripts. Text output is unchanged for both. Adds renderer unit tests.

## Test plan

- `go test ./op-challenger/cmd/ -run TestRender`
- Manually verified against live ink-mainnet games: `--format json`, default text (unchanged), and invalid `--format` rejected — for both subcommands.

topPRs.title: rust: centralize OP fork → implied L1 fork mapping
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Implements the plan from #21338 (see the [investigation comment](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21338#issuecomment-4693050388)):

- **Canonical table**: `OpHardfork::activates_l1_fork()` in `alloy-op-hardforks` is now the single source of the OP fork → implied L1 fork relation, with two derived views: `implied_l1_fork()` (cumulative) and `activating_op_fork()` (range-aware inverse: the earliest OP fork whose implied L1 fork covers the queried one, so Bedrock activates the whole pre-merge range up to Paris). A monotonicity test and an inverse round-trip test lock its shape.
- **Rewired consumers** (all previously hand-maintained copies):
  - `alloy-op-hardforks`: `OpChainHardforks`' `EthereumHardforks`/`Index<EthereumHardfork>` impls (the `unreachable!()` for unmapped L1 forks is gone — unknown forks now resolve to `Never`)
  - `kona-genesis`: `EthereumHardforks for RollupConfig` — **fixes the latent missing `Karst → Osaka` mapping** (Osaka returned `Never` even with `karst_time` set); red/green regression test included. The range-aware inverse also subsumes the special London-through-Paris branch here and in `OpChainHardforks`' `Index`.
  - `op-reth` chainspec: builder `*_activated()` helpers (collapsed onto one table-driven helper), `From<Genesis>` L1 timestamp derivation, and superchain `chain_metadata`
  - `kona-engine`: the three engine API version selectors are now keyed purely off implied L1 fork activations — a future OP fork that implies a new L1 fork needs zero changes there
- **op-revm**: keeps its hand-written `OpSpecId::into_eth_spec` (deliberately no alloy deps); a consistency test in `alloy-op-evm` — the one crate depending on both — pins it to the canonical table so divergence fails CI.
- **Karst schedule**: adds the already-scheduled Karst activation (constants existed, schedules didn't) to `OpHardfork::op_mainnet/op_sepolia` and op-reth's `OP_MAINNET_HARDFORKS`/`OP_SEPOLIA_HARDFORKS`, aligning op-reth's fork schedule and P2P fork IDs with op-geth/superchain-registry. Base has no Karst constants yet and is untouched.

## Impact of the kona-genesis fix

The Osaka gap was latent: no code path called `EthereumHardforks` methods on `RollupConfig` (kona-client derives its EVM spec via `OpHardforks`/`spec_id`, which was always correct), so shipped kona-client Karst releases are unaffected. It becomes load-bearing in this PR, since kona-engine now queries L1 forks on `RollupConfig`.

## Test plan

- Red/green: the new `test_ethereum_fork_activation_follows_op_forks` fails on the baseline (`Osaka → Never`) and passes with the fix.
- New tests: canonical table + monotonicity + inverse round-trip (alloy-op-hardforks), L1↔OP activation equality on real schedules, engine version selection for all three methods (kona-engine), op-revm↔table consistency (alloy-op-evm), Karst schedule/reverse-lookup cases.
- `cargo nextest run` for all five touched crates (310 tests) ✅, `cargo check --workspace --tests --all-features` ✅, `just check-no-std` ✅, clippy `-D warnings` ✅, `just fmt-check` ✅.

Closes #21338

topPRs.title: fix(alloy-op-evm): roll back SDM block-warming for declined op-rbuilder candidates
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Fixes: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21354
Test disabled at: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21337

## Summary

`TestFlashblocksSDMMaterializesPostExecBlock` was skipped in #21337 after it failed under Osaka (Karst) with a 9-vs-15 post-exec gas-refund **entry-count** mismatch. Investigating that failure split it into two distinct findings:

1. **The 9-vs-15 CI failure itself was a test-harness flake, not an op-rbuilder bug** — op-rbuilder's block was correct.
2. **A separate, genuine producer↔derivation divergence does exist** — phantom SDM block-warming from declined builder candidates — which the flaky test was *not* actually catching.

This PR fixes the real divergence (alloy-op-evm), de-flakes and re-enables the test, and adds a dedicated test that pins the real divergence end-to-end.

## Root cause

### 1. The reported 9-vs-15 mismatch was a test capture-race, not a divergence

Issue #21354 framed the failure as op-rbuilder over-accumulating refunds and diverging from op-node's derivation under Osaka. That framing doesn't hold up against the assertion that actually failed:

- The two sides compared at the failing line are **not** "op-node vs op-rbuilder". They are op-rbuilder's own **streamed flashblock snapshot** (`observed.payload`, the 9-entry side) vs the **sealed canonical block** read back from the sequencer EL (the 15-entry side). op-node's derivation (`ValidatePostExecBlock`) runs *after* that line and never executed.
- The per-tx refund was identical (`0xd4e4`) on every entry on both sides — only the **count** differed. So it was never a refund-math/accumulation bug; it was "how many txs the snapshot had seen so far".
- Post-exec entries accumulate monotonically across a block's flashblocks, and flashblocks carry no `is_final` flag. The test guessed which flashblock was "final". Under Osaka, calldata repricing packs more txs per block → more flashblocks per block → a wider window in which the test latches `observed` on a stale, in-progress flashblock (9) and compares it against the fully-sealed block (15). Fast hosts win the race (green 19/19 locally); loaded CI loses it.

So op-rbuilder produced the correct block; Osaka only widened the timing window. **This part is fixed in the test, not in op-rbuilder** — by matching the streamed flashblock to the sealed block by canonical hash instead of guessing the final one.

### 2. The real divergence: phantom SDM warming from declined candidates

While building coverage that would *actually* exercise producer-vs-derivation, a real divergence surfaced. SDM block-warming refunds are recorded by an inspector during EVM execution — *before* the builder's commit decision — and are **not** journaled, so discarding a tx's changes does not roll them back. The op-rbuilder payload builder (standard and flashblocks) selects txs via `execute_transaction_with_commit_condition` and **declines** candidates (`CommitChanges::No`) that exceed a builder gas/DA/address limit or are reverted-and-excluded. A declined candidate still warmed the maps, so a later *committed* tx could claim a block-warming refund attributed to a tx that never entered the block.

Commit-only paths — block import and `debug_replaySDMBlock` derivation — only ever commit txs, so they never observe that phantom warmth and derive a strictly smaller refund set. The producer's payload then genuinely diverges from derivation. This is independent of Osaka and is the bug worth fixing in the builder/EVM.

## The fix

- **`rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs`** — override `execute_transaction_with_commit_condition` on `OpBlockExecutor`: snapshot the block-scoped warming state before execution and restore it whenever the tx is not committed. The snapshot (a clone of the warming maps) is taken only in `Producing` mode, so there's no clone cost when SDM is off or verifying.
- **`rust/op-rbuilder/.../builders/context.rs`** — comment at the decline site documenting that `CommitChanges::No` relies on the alloy-op-evm rollback.

## Tests

- **`flashblocks_sdm_phantom_test.go`** (new) — `TestFlashblocksSDMPhantomWarmingDivergence` reproduces finding #2: a persistently-declined poisoner (over `--builder.max_gas_per_txn`) alongside committed victims, comparing each victim block's producer-baked SDM payload against the commit-only derivation. FAILS on develop (divergent_blocks=6, victim refund 18400 vs derived 0); PASSES with the fix (divergent_blocks=0).
- **`alloy-op-evm/src/block/tests.rs`** — unit test for the declined-candidate warming rollback in isolation.
- **`flashblocks_sdm_test.go`** — re-enables `TestFlashblocksSDMMaterializesPostExecBlock` (removes the `t.Skip`) and fixes finding #1: replaces the flaky "final flashblock" heuristic (and its 15s deadline backstop) with an identity match by canonical block hash (`observedByHash`). The sealed block is looked up by hash among streamed flashblocks; a miss after op-rbuilder has advanced past the block fails loudly (EL fallback / builder stream ≠ seal) rather than racing.

## Notes

SDM rides Interop (Lagoon), which is not activated on any chain in the near term, so neither the flake nor the divergence was user-facing.

topPRs.title: alloy-op-evm: reject user txs in fork-activation blocks (forks ≥ Jovian)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/553

## Summary

A **fork-activation block** — the first L2 block at/after a fork's activation timestamp — must contain only deposit transactions (the L1-attributes deposit + the network-upgrade automatic deposits), no user transactions. op-geth enforces this at the executor / consensus-validity layer (`CalcDAFootprint`), but the shared Rust executor (`alloy-op-evm`, used by **both op-reth and kona-client**) was missing it — a latent consensus-validity divergence where op-reth / kona-client would *accept* an activation block containing user txs that op-geth *rejects*.

No live exploit: Jovian's canonical activation block on OP Mainnet contains no user txs. Also, the batch validity rule is already there, so it's enforced for the safe chain already.

## What this does

- Adds a fork-activation-block guard to the shared `OpBlockExecutor`: on the first block of a fork at or after Jovian, any non-deposit (user) tx is rejected with `OpBlockExecutionError::UnexpectedNonDepositTxInForkActivationBlock`.
- Detects the activation block from the parent timestamp via a new required `OpBlockExecutionCtx::parent_timestamp: Option<u64>`: a block is the first block of fork `F` when `is_F_active(block_ts) && !is_F_active(parent_ts)`, iterated over `OpHardfork::Jovian.forks_from()` so the rule covers Jovian, Karst, Lagoon and any future fork automatically.
- Adds `OpHardfork::forks_from()` to `alloy-op-hardforks` (a go-ethereum `forks.From` analogue).
- Populates `parent_timestamp` where the parent header is available: kona `StatelessL2Builder` (the fault-proof path) and op-reth's block-building path. On op-reth's block-import / engine-`newPayload` paths the parent header isn't available at executor-context construction, so `parent_timestamp` is `None` and the executor skips the check — that path is covered by the derivation layer (op-node + kona drop user-tx batches in fork-activation blocks).

### Why parent-timestamp rather than op-geth's length-based detection

op-geth detects the *Jovian* activation block via the Isthmus-length L1-attributes tx (the DA-footprint scalar isn't set yet) — Jovian-specific, and Karst/Lagoon reuse the Jovian attributes format so there's no length signal. op-geth is also deprecated at Karst (`karstKillSwitch`), so for Karst+ op-reth and kona-client are the consensus reference. The parent-timestamp "first block of fork" rule is the fork-agnostic, spec-accurate definition and matches the derivation layer.

## Follow-up

Unifying the derivation/batch-validity rule (kona `single.rs`, op-node `batches.go`, which still hard-code the fork list) onto the same dynamic `forks_from` form is tracked in ethereum-optimism/optimism-private#555.

## Testing

- New `alloy-op-evm` unit tests, looping over `forks_from(Jovian)` so future forks are exercised automatically: activation block + user tx → rejected; deposits-only → accepted; normal post-activation block + user tx → accepted; `parent_timestamp = None` → check skipped; non-activation block → not flagged. Plus a `forks_from` test in `alloy-op-hardforks`.
- Built + tested every affected crate: `alloy-op-evm`, `alloy-op-hardforks`, `reth-optimism-evm`, `reth-optimism-consensus`, `reth-optimism-payload-builder`, `reth-optimism-node`, the op-reth custom-node example, `kona-executor` (incl. real-mainnet-block stateless execution), `kona-client`. `cargo +nightly fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
